-- January 3, 1989

The Treutlen County Board of Commissioners met in regular session on the above date with Commissioners Gillis, Sherrod, McLendon, and Warnock being present.

Commissioner Smith was absent. The minutes of the December 6, 1988 meeting were approved as read. Old business discussed is as follows:

- 1. Commissioner Gillis made a motion to issue Beer License to Edward Nobles, dba/Lakeside Club, effective January 6, 1989 at which time Mr. Nobles will turn 21 years of age. Commissioner McLendon seconded. All voted in favor.

- 2. Commissioner Warnock made a motion that the Beer License Ordinance be amended to change the age from 18 to 21 years old before being eligible to be considered for a beer license.

- 3. Commissioner McLendon reported that the contractor who cuts the right-of-way for REA would be interested in cutting the county right-of-ways. There would be two men at $10.00 per hour each and the ewuipment would be $15.00 per hour. No action taken.

- 4. Reopening of County Road #103 discussed. No action taken.

- 5. Chamber of Commerce budget for the 1989 year was discussed. Commissioner Warnock made a motion that the Commissioners table the decision until the City makes their decision. Commissioner McLendon seconded. All voted in favor.

- 6. Commissioner Warnock .reported that he had talked with Mr. Winford Smith with the Georgia Power Company about the lights on the Walking Trail and that Mr. Smith will furnish an old pole for the light. Mr. Smith suggested a 400 watt sodium light be used. The cost per month would’ be $19.20. - Commissioner Warnock made a motion that since this is a project by the Year 2,000 Group that the county and city jointly pay for the lighting and Georgia Power send the billing to the County. Commissioner Sherrod seconded. All voted in favor.

- 7. The outside lighting at the Health Department. Commissioner Warnock reported that Mr. Winford Smith with the Georgia Power Company had suggested a 400 watt sodium directional light to replace the present 175 watt mercury light. Georgia Power will need a letter requesting said change and stating who will be responsible for payment of lighting. The monthly cost will be $19.20. Commissioner Sherrod made a motion that a 400 watt sodium directional light be installed and the county will be responsible for paying the monthly bill. Commissioner Warnock seconded. All voted in favor.

Mr. Harold McLendon presented a quote to the Commissioners to serve as Public Defender for the courts for the 1989 calendar year. Mr. McLendon's quote was for $10,000.00 annually. Commissioner McLendon made a motion that the Commissioenrs request Judge Towson to set up a three person committee to. appoint the Public Defender and the appointment be made by or before Apri 1, 1989. The present contract will be extended until March 31, 1989. - Commissioner Warnock seconded. All voted in favor.

May 2, 1989

The Treutlen County Board of Commissioners met in regular session on the above date with Commissioners Gillis, Sherrod, McLendon and Smith being present. Commissioner Warnock was unable to attend.

The minutes of the April 4, 1989 meeting were approved.

Chairman Gillis read the Landfill Inspection Report to the Commissioners. There is a problem with erosion which needs to be corrected. Commissioner Sherrod made a motion that Chairman Gillis and Wheeler County Commissioner Maurice Johnson go ahead and make the corrections required by the Inspection Report. Commissioner McLendon seconded. All agreed.

Commissioner Smith made a motion that Treutlen County allow Dodge County to have sponsorship of the Summer Food Program for the Youth which is through the United States Department of Agriculture; and Dodge County would implement the program in Treutlen County at no cost to this county. Commissioner Sherrod seconded. All voted in favor.

Commissioner McLendon made a motion that the Resolution Requiring Permit For Installation of On-Site Sewage Management Systems Requiring Decal For Mobile Homes Before Location or Relocating be run in the Soperton News for 4 weeks, a copy of the Resolution be mailed to the Georgia Power Company, Altamaha Electric Membership Corporation, and all mobile home dealers in Swainsboro, Dublin and Vidalia. Commissioner Sherrod seconded. All agreed.

Commissioner Smith made a motion that Mark Burns, Tax Appraiser give the County Commissioners a copy of the list of mobile homes and new houses picked up to go on the tax digest. Commissioner Sherrod seconded. All voted in favor.

Commissioner Sherrod made a motion that a view of the fact that the County is contributing $75.00 per week to the Chamber of Commerce for a secretary that a monthly activity report be sent to the County Commissioners. Commissioner McLendon seconded. All approved.

Commissioner Smith seconded. All voted in favor.

Treutlen County Commissioners Amendment to Beer License of Treutlen County, Georgia

On motion made and duly séconded, the following amendment was adopted to amend to the Treutlen County Beer Ordinance as follows:

To amend Section 6 to add a new paragraph number 6. (a 1) as follows

6(a 1) The Clerk shall cause to be published in the official Gazette of the County, once-a-week during the two weeks immediately preceding the date of the meeting at which the application is scheduled for consideration by the Commissioners, a notice which shall include the name and address of the applicant, the location for which the license is sought, the type of license applied for, and the time and place the application will be considered by the Commissioners.

Unanimously adopted this 6th day of September 1 1994, Chairman, Commissioners of Treutlen County, Ga. Attest:
